key_insight: Adaptive mesh neural operators need to decide not only where to place computation, but also how to make representations comparable after nodes move; GA-AMNO adds gauge-aware transport to make both steps operator-readable.
engineering_relevance: The method improves PDE surrogate accuracy on nonuniform and geometrically mismatched meshes, making adaptive neural solvers more reliable for real-world simulations with changing discretizations.
method: Physics-informed adaptive allocation chooses where to compute on the mesh.
Geometry-conditioned low-rank Gauge transport aligns source and target features before aggregation.
The framework provides conditions for representation-consistent aggregation and analyzes transport error/continuity.
evidence_signal: Across five PDE benchmarks, the paper reports improved predictive accuracy, with controlled interventions and geometric-mismatch tests showing better cross-discretization compatibility.
watch_item: Gauge transport adds modeling and implementation complexity, and its benefits may depend on accurate geometry conditioning and topology-preserving mesh deformations.
paper_title: Where to Compute and How to Interact: Operator-Readable Adaptation with Gauge-Aware Transport
